items.headline: Update: Singapore and Indonesia agree to set up joint haze task force and share data
items.summary: Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan and his Indonesian counterpart agreed to create a joint task force on the Indonesian forest fires and to share data, as Minister K. Shanmugam said Singapore expects to table haze legislation in Parliament next week.

items.headline: Singapore construction firm charged over unlicensed foreign-worker dormitory
items.summary: Construction company LBD Engineering and its general manager were charged on Oct 29 with operating an unlicensed dormitory for foreign workers in Sungei Kadut, under the Foreign Employee Dormitories Act.

items.headline: As haze chokes Singapore, runners swap the streets for shopping malls
items.summary: With the 24-hour PSI pushed into unhealthy territory by transboundary haze, Singapore runners moved their training indoors to shopping malls and gyms, and several outdoor races were rescheduled.

items.headline: Temasek and GIC reject claims they engineered Indonesia's market rout
items.summary: Temasek's Asia-Pacific head Fock Wai Hoong called a former Indonesian trade minister's allegation that the two state investors lobbied MSCI to downgrade Jakarta's market “patently untrue”; GIC said its decisions are driven by company fundamentals, not index status.

items.headline: Jamia student enters 18th day of hunger strike to revive a 20-year-suspended union
items.summary: Law student Ebin Basil pressed an 18-day hunger strike demanding Jamia Millia Islamia restore its students' union, suspended for about 20 years; the Delhi campus has been shut with classes moved online until Jan 13.

items.headline: India says its forces are in multiple face-offs with China in Arunachal Pradesh
items.summary: A border force chief said Indian and Chinese troops are locked in several ongoing standoffs along the Arunachal Pradesh frontier, six years after the deadly 2020 Galwan Valley clash.

items.headline: Modi stays under pressure as 'cockroach' voter-roll protests and court petitions mount
items.summary: The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party and the opposition INDIA bloc are staging near-daily protests demanding the Election Commission chief resign over a voter-roll revision that removed about 130 million entries; the opposition has petitioned the Supreme Court to halt it.

items.headline: Update: Clean-up begins in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha after deadly Cyclone Arnab
items.summary: Rescue and clean-up operations were under way across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha after Cyclone Arnab's landfall, which killed at least three people and forced about 180,000 to evacuate from the two states.

items.headline: Update: Markets reward Healey's Budget as gilts rally and bank shares climb
items.summary: UK gilts gained and London lenders rose after Chancellor John Healey's first Budget, with the 10-year yield around 5.32% and Barclays up 3.3% and Lloyds up 2.6%, as investors judged the bank and gambling taxes milder than feared.

items.headline: Healey defends his first Budget and warns of 'tough decisions' still ahead
items.summary: A day after the Budget, Chancellor John Healey defended the package and cautioned that harder fiscal choices lie ahead, with the OBR putting fiscal headroom at about £15bn by 2029-30.

items.headline: UK mortgage approvals fall to a 33-month low as borrowing costs bite
items.summary: UK mortgage approvals dropped more than forecast in September to their lowest since December 2023, as elevated loan costs weighed on the housing market ahead of an expected Bank of England move.

items.headline: Burnham helps Labour to its biggest poll bounce in 70 years at the 100-day mark
items.summary: Bloomberg reported Labour has posted one of the largest popularity jumps for any party that changed prime minister mid-parliament in over 70 years, with a late Survation poll putting Labour near 29% against Reform UK on about 23%.

items.headline: Obama and Trump trade blows at rival rallies days before the US midterms
items.summary: Former president Barack Obama and President Donald Trump headlined duelling rallies in Georgia and Ohio on Oct 29, sharpening attacks six days before the Nov 3 midterm elections with more than 30 million early ballots already cast.

items.headline: North Korea fires about 10 short-range ballistic missiles amid a landmine dispute
items.summary: South Korea's Joint Chiefs said North Korea launched roughly 10 short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan into the Sea of Japan on Oct 29, as tensions rose over a DMZ landmine blast; Japan said the missiles fell outside its exclusive economic zone.

items.headline: Russian strikes kill at least 19 in Ukraine, 14 at a Dnipro train station
items.summary: Russian attacks across Ukraine killed at least 19 people, including 14 at a crowded platform in Dnipro's main railway station, after Ukraine launched a large overnight drone barrage toward the Moscow region.

items.headline: Israeli strikes kill six in Gaza as officials press to reopen the Rafah crossing
items.summary: Gaza's Health Ministry reported six people killed and dozens wounded over 24 hours, including a drone strike in Maghazi refugee camp, and urged the reopening of the Rafah crossing despite the year-old ceasefire.

items.headline: US military strike on an alleged drug boat kills five in the eastern Pacific
items.summary: US Southern Command said an Oct 27 strike killed five people on a vessel it alleged was trafficking drugs; Al Jazeera put the campaign's toll at about 243 across roughly 70 strikes in the Caribbean and Pacific.

items.headline: Upwind raises $400 million after walking away from a Datadog takeover
items.summary: Cloud-security startup Upwind closed a $400 million Series C led by Bessemer Venture Partners at a $3.8 billion valuation, after turning down a Datadog acquisition offer that carried no premium; it is on track for about $90 million in annual recurring revenue.

items.headline: Wabi, an AI agent that builds mini-apps, is now valued at $1.25 billion
items.summary: Wabi, led by Replika founder Eugenia Kuyda, raised $55 million led by IVP, with a16z and the Amazon Alexa Fund, at a $1.25 billion valuation for its “personal agent” that generates small task-specific apps.

items.headline: Google rolls out ads in AI Mode internationally as search ad growth slows
items.summary: On its Q3 earnings call Google said it is extending ads in AI Mode to international markets; Alphabet posted $127.6 billion in revenue but Search revenue growth slowed to 12% from 17% a quarter earlier, and the shares fell about 8%.

items.headline: SuperMe raises $20 million for a network of paid AI expert profiles
items.summary: SuperMe raised $20 million led by Forerunner's Kirsten Green, with Greylock, to build a network of AI clones of human experts; the service is free for now but plans to cap the number of questions users can ask.

items.headline: Amazon jumps as AWS growth tops 39%, outpacing cloud rivals
items.summary: Amazon reported third-quarter AWS revenue growing more than 39% year over year, ahead of expectations, with AWS operating income of $17.8 billion up from $11.4 billion a year earlier; the shares surged after hours.

items.headline: Samsung posts its first-ever 100-trillion-won quarterly profit, but shares slip
items.summary: Samsung Electronics reported record third-quarter operating profit of 107.44 trillion won, its first quarter above 100 trillion won, driven by HBM4 and server SSD demand, yet the stock still closed about 4.1% lower.

items.headline: Shell nearly doubles quarterly profit to $10.8 billion on record refining margins
items.summary: Shell's third-quarter adjusted earnings nearly doubled year on year to $10.81 billion, its strongest since mid-2022, as indicative refining margins hit a record of about $42 a barrel amid Middle East supply disruption.

items.headline: Lagarde to step down as ECB president early, triggering a succession race
items.summary: Christine Lagarde said she will leave the European Central Bank presidency early, ahead of her term's October 2027 end, on the day the ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5% with euro-area inflation at 3.8%.

items.headline: Eli Lilly jumps after a big earnings beat and raised revenue outlook
items.summary: Eli Lilly reported adjusted earnings of $7.48 a share against $6.26 expected and lifted its 2026 revenue guidance to $91-92 billion from $85-87 billion; the shares rose about 7%.

items.headline: 🏎️ Antonelli misses Mexico City media day with a viral illness before likely title
items.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli, 123 points clear, pulled out of Thursday media duties in Mexico City with a viral illness; a top-nine finish on Sunday would make him Formula 1's youngest world champion at 20.

items.headline: 🏎️ McLaren plan fresh upgrades for Mexico after Norris and Piastri struggle in Austin
items.summary: McLaren will bring more upgrades to the Mexico City Grand Prix after Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri underperformed at the US Grand Prix, where Antonelli's win moved him to the brink of the drivers' title.

items.headline: 🎾 Arthur Fils rallies past Michelsen to reach the Basel quarter-finals
items.summary: Second seed Arthur Fils beat Alex Michelsen 4-6, 6-3, 7-6(5) to reach the Swiss Indoors Basel quarter-finals and boost his hopes of a Turin ATP Finals debut; he next meets sixth seed Taylor Fritz.

items.headline: 🎾 Ben Shelton blasts 44 aces to survive a first-round scare in Basel
items.summary: Top seed Ben Shelton fired 44 aces to edge Aleksandar Kovacevic 6-7(4), 7-6(3), 7-6(4) in his Swiss Indoors Basel opener, saving his tournament in just under three hours.

items.headline: Prime editing used to rewrite DNA inside the human body for the first time
items.summary: Prime Medicine said it dosed the first patient in an in-body prime-editing trial for Wilson's disease, rewriting DNA in liver cells to fix a mutation that lets copper build up; it expects first results next year.

items.headline: Physicists trap a single antimatter particle for a month, opening new-physics tests
items.summary: Gerald Gabrielse's Northwestern team suspended a single positron in a “one-positron quantum cyclotron” for about a month, aiming to measure its magnetic moment with enough precision to probe physics beyond the Standard Model; the work appeared in Physical Review Letters.

items.headline: A Jurassic swimmer reveals the origin of the mammalian throat 165 million years ago
items.summary: Nature described Megacauda, the largest known Jurassic mammaliaform, a platypus-like swimmer from Inner Mongolia whose exquisitely preserved throat shows a pharynx that let early mammal relatives suckle and swallow.

items.headline: NASA's Lucy becomes the first spacecraft to reach Jupiter's Trojan asteroids
items.summary: Five years and more than 2.2 billion miles after its October 2021 launch, NASA's Lucy entered the Jupiter Trojan asteroid region; its first flyby, of the asteroid Eurybates, is set for Aug 11, 2027.

items.headline: NASA's Voyager 1 resolves a brief communications pause and conserves power
items.summary: Voyager 1 fell silent during two scheduled contacts on Oct 18-19 before its signal returned on Oct 20; engineers tied it to an automatic thruster swap, and a September power-saving move should extend the 1977 probe's science.

fun_fact.headline: Scotland's national animal is the mythical unicorn
fun_fact.body: Scotland's national animal is not a real creature at all — it is the unicorn. The mythical beast was embraced as a royal symbol in medieval Scotland and still appears, shown bound in a golden chain, on the United Kingdom's royal coat of arms. In heraldry the unicorn stood for purity and untameable strength, and a chained one signalled a power so wild that only a king could master it.
fun_fact.source: VisitScotland; National Trust for Scotland; History Hit

puzzle.title: Hole Punch
puzzle.body:
Take a square sheet of paper.
Fold it exactly in half from left to right.
Then fold that result exactly in half from top to bottom.
You are now holding a smaller square that is four layers thick.
Punch one round hole straight through all four layers, somewhere in the middle of the folded square (not on either folded edge).
Now unfold the paper completely.

How many holes are in the sheet, and how are they arranged?
puzzle.approach: Track how many layers the punch goes through, then reflect the hole across each fold line as you mentally unfold the sheet.
puzzle.answer:
Four holes.

Two folds stack the paper into four layers, so a single punch pierces four layers and makes four holes. The folds run along the vertical centre line and the horizontal centre line of the full sheet, so unfolding reflects the one punched hole across both of those lines. The result is one hole in each quadrant — a symmetric 2×2 pattern, mirror-balanced about the centre of the sheet.

word_puzzle.title: Base Metal
word_puzzle.body:
Turn LEAD into GOLD in three steps.
Change exactly one letter at a time, and every step must be a valid English word.

LEAD → _ _ _ _ → _ _ _ _ → GOLD
word_puzzle.approach: Change exactly one letter at each step, and make sure every rung is a real English word. Three steps get you there.
word_puzzle.answer:
LEAD → LOAD → GOAD → GOLD

LEAD→LOAD (change E to O), LOAD→GOAD (change L to G; a goad is a pointed stick used to prod cattle), GOAD→GOLD (change A to L).
